items.stem: Which of the following best describes "aim of an exploration"?
options: A one-hour paper of two extended problems (55 marks) in which students develop and interpret a model in an unfamiliar context
The extent of the investigation: narrow enough to treat in depth within 12–20 pages, broad enough to use mathematics commensurate with the course
A clear, focused statement of what the exploration sets out to investigate or answer
Critical reflection on results, methods, limitations and links (maximum 3 marks)
items.answer: A clear, focused statement of what the exploration sets out to investigate or answer
items.markingKey: C. "aim of an exploration" is a clear, focused statement of what the exploration sets out to investigate or answer.

items.stem: A student's proposed exploration title is "Human bodies". Explain why this needs refining and suggest a focused aim using correlation, regression and t-tests.
items.answer: e.g. "To investigate the relationship between height and arm span in my class using correlation, regression and t-tests."
items.markingKey: R1 the title is too broad/vague to explore in depth; R1 a focused aim states the specific question and method; A1 e.g. "To investigate the relationship between height and arm span in my class using correlation, regression and t-tests", with data: measure classmates with consent.

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why a focused aim is important in the exploration.
items.answer: A focused aim gives the exploration direction, allows depth rather than superficial coverage and lets the student judge whether the aim was achieved in the conclusion. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: A focused aim gives the exploration direction, allows depth rather than superficial coverage and lets the student judge whether the aim was achieved in the conclusion. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Tomás writes: "The exploration should cover as many topics from the course as possible." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Depth matters more than breadth: a focused exploration using relevant mathematics well scores higher than a superficial survey.
items.markingKey: Depth matters more than breadth: a focused exploration using relevant mathematics well scores higher than a superficial survey. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Two students submit aims. Student P: "To investigate the fairness of a local lottery using probability, expected value and χ² tests, based on data where I record past draw results." Student Q: "My exploration is about maths on the road." Evaluate the two aims and suggest how Student Q could improve theirs.
items.answer: P is focused and testable; Q is too vague
items.markingKey: R1 P names a specific question, the mathematics (probability, expected value and χ² tests) and a data source; R1 Q gives no question, method or data; A1 e.g. "To investigate the optimal route for a delivery driver in my town using graph theory: travelling salesman bounds"; R1 Q should also say how data will be obtained (measure road distances between the delivery points).

items.stem: Analyse one strength and one limitation of this view: "Choosing a well-known textbook topic (e.g. the golden ratio) is a safe choice for the exploration."
items.answer: It can work only if the student adds a genuinely personal angle or data; otherwise a more personal, focused question is better.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: plenty of sources; mathematics is accessible. Arguments against: hard to show personal engagement; often reproduces existing work without new insight. Supported judgement: It can work only if the student adds a genuinely personal angle or data; otherwise a more personal, focused question is better.

(d) Explain why the use of mathematics (criterion E) carries the largest weighting. (e) The current scores are A2, B1, C2, D1, E4; find the total and the maximum possible gain.
items.answer: (a) B, E, D (e) 10/20; gain up to 10

(c) A1 B: 4, D: 3, E: 6. (d) R1 E (6 marks) rewards the correct, relevant and sophisticated mathematics that is the core of the exploration. (e) A1 10, 10.
